A graphic designer is reducing the diagonals of a simple square on the screen at a rate of $2.5\text{ mm}\text{/s}.$ At what rate, in squared millimeters per second, is the area of the square decreasing when the length of the diagonal is $12.4\,\text{mm}?$

feedback.problem:

A robotics system is expanding a square inspection window by increasing the lengths of its diagonals at a rate of $2.4\text{ mm}\text{/s}.$ At what rate is the area of the window increasing when each diagonal measures $10\,\text{mm}?$

The area is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}} ${\text{mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $h$ and $A$ be the length of the diagonals and the area of the square, respectively. Using the Pythagorean theorem, it can be shown that the relationship between $A$ and $h$ is

$$
A=\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}.
$$

We want to find

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}h}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot h.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $h$ increases at a rate of $2.4\,\text{mm/s},$ so

$$
\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}=2.4.
$$

Also, we want to compute the rate of change of the area when the diagonal has length $h=10.$ Substituting this information into our expression for $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =2.4\cdot 10=24{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the area of the square inspection window is increasing at a rate of 
$24{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.$
